nodes.text: LiteLLM treats context-window overflow and content-policy rejection as dedicated fallback triggers (context_window_fallbacks for ContextWindowExceededError, content_policy_fallbacks for ContentPolicyViolationError), mapped across providers; the documented use is falling back to another model or provider. This is evidence against a blanket 'never fall back on caller errors such as 400 or context length'.
nodes.applicability: LiteLLM proxy/router, a vendor gateway; fallback goes to a different model group (larger window, other provider), not a retry of the same request.
nodes.limitations: Page gives no guidance on when fallback is unwise (e.g. for caller bugs); only the existence and intent of the chains.

nodes.text: Pydantic AI FallbackModel's default trigger is ModelAPIError (4xx/5xx and pre-response connection failures/timeouts), explicitly including rejected requests such as bad credentials, rejected model name and context-window overflow, on the reasoning that another model may accept what the first rejected.
nodes.limitations: Describes the default; it is configurable, so it is not a recommendation to fall back on every 4xx.

nodes.text: Refinement of the fallback policy: context-length (and content-policy) errors are fallback-worthy only when the fallback target differs in a way that can fix them (larger window, other provider policy); generic 4xx caller errors (malformed request, auth on the same credential) are not fixed by another model. Both LiteLLM and Pydantic AI treat context overflow as a fallback case, so @C45 should be narrowed to 'not on caller bugs', not 'not on context length'.

Google ADK 1.24.0 changed DatabaseSessionService.append_event() from raising ValueError on a stale session to reloading the session and appending anyway; with two concurrent run_async calls on one session this interleaves events, the LLM sees duplicate/contradictory tool calls and responses, and history is corrupted. Reported affected versions >=1.24.0 (1.24.0, 1.25.0, 1.26.0); last working 1.23.0.
nodes.limitations: Single user issue report (reproduction by the author), not a maintainer-confirmed analysis on the page fetched. Scenario is two servers resuming one session; a single-process host serialising turns per session avoids it.

nodes.text: ADK issue #4771 reports that overlapping requests on one session (a new turn arriving while the previous turn still writes events) make the new turn start with missing session state; a maintainer notes concurrent append_event() writes can trigger OCC aborts even on pure reads (Spanner dialect). Page does not mention duplicate tool calls; those are in #4751.
nodes.limitations: Dialect-specific; second independent report of concurrent-turn problems in ADK.

nodes.text: ADK PR #4752 (optimistic concurrency via an event sequence number, rejecting stale updates with 'The session has been modified in storage. Please reload the session before appending events.') was closed unmerged on 2026-07-06; the maintainer closed it saying #4751 was already fixed in main by commit b8e7647. The content of that fix was not verified (commit page returned HTTP 503).
nodes.limitations: Fix commit not read; whether main restored the ValueError on stale sessions is unverified.

nodes.text: Concurrent turns on one persisted session are a recurring failure source across frameworks (ADK stale-session reload-and-continue; OpenAI SDK concurrent add_items deletion), so a single-process library should serialise turns per session (or use a version check on save) rather than rely on the storage layer.

OpenAI Agents SDK MCPServerManager defaults connect_timeout_seconds=10.0 and cleanup_timeout_seconds=10.0 (None disables, zero rejected), with strict=False, drop_failed_servers=True and connect_in_parallel=False. This is a manager-level connect timeout, distinct from the 5 s client_session_timeout_seconds per-request timeout in @C42.
nodes.limitations: Reference page for the version current on 2026-11-20.

nodes.text: Pydantic v2 ser_json_bytes and val_json_bytes both default to 'utf8' (options utf8, base64, hex); to get an equal value after a serialise/validate round trip they must be set equal. val_json_bytes was added in v2.9. With the utf8 default, arbitrary (non-UTF-8) bytes do not round-trip safely, so persisted conversation JSON containing bytes should use base64 on both sides.
nodes.limitations: The last sentence (non-UTF-8 bytes) is our inference from the utf8 description, not a quoted statement.
